Exposure to loud tra�c noises was compared in two groups. 20 patients and ten controls had such an exposure. Which of the following is

questions.question_text:
In a case-control study of possible nutritional correlates of depression, subjects were asked about the frequency of consuming 20 di�erent
food items in a Likert scale. The histories of cases di�ered signi�cantly from those of controls, at p=.05, for three of the 20 listed items.
Which of the following is most likely?

options.text: The study is inconclusive: further case control studies with more rigorous methods are required
Diet is related to depression; but it is unclear which of the three items is the most important culprit
Diet is not related to depression as the results are due to chance �nding: discard the study
The results are conclusive if it could be shown that there was no recall bias
Diet is de�nitely related to depression; further cohort studies for each of the 3 items are warranted

correct_answer.text: The study is inconclusive: further case control studies with more rigorous methods are required

questions.explanation:
There are two important problems with this study. Asking depressed subjects to recall numerous food items can produce serious recall bias.
In addition, at a signi�cance level of 0.05, at least one out of the 20 items may show an association by chance. As it is di�cult to say which of
the three items are really associated with depression, it may not be wise to invest huge e�ort and money in a cohort study at this stage. It is
best if a more rigorous case-control study is attempted to replicate or refute the �ndings.

questions.question_text:
A case-control study investigating various risk factors for a disease in hospitalised patients chooses healthy relatives of the patients as
controls. In which of the following situations the results may be distorted?

options.text: Risk factor is related to diet and lifestyle
Risk factor is purely related to occupational exposure
Disease is not shared by families
Exposure is likely to be not shared by families
Risk factor is not related to household environment

correct_answer.text: Risk factor is related to diet and lifestyle

questions.explanation:
This matching approach increases the likelihood that the factors that are generally shared by family members will be similar for both the
controls and the cases. This reduces bias and confounding especially if the cause of a disease is not shared in families. Unfortunately in
cases where the causal agent is genetic or otherwise familial, this method leads to "overmatching" thus reducing the ability to demonstrate
the causation.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following types of bias is NOT a major concern in a hospital-based case-control study?
questions.explanation:
Work up bias (veri�cation bias) refers to a systematic error in the assessment of the validity of a diagnostic test. When the execution of the
gold standard is in�uenced by the results of the assessed test, especially when the reference test is less frequently performed when the
assessed test result is negative, then this will in�uence the number of false negatives correctly identi�ed in the exercise. This bias is speci�c
to assessment of diagnostic tests and so not seen in ordinary case-control studies where cases and controls are determined before
estimates of exposure begin. Family aggregation bias is a type of information bias wherein presence of a case in the family increases
awareness of risk factors and exposure leading to more family members of cases reporting an exposure though controls have family
members with less awareness. Journal Epid Comm Health 2004;58;635-641

questions.question_text: Which of the following describes the relationship between prevalence and incidence rates?
questions.explanation:
In a steady-state situation, in which the rates are not changing, and in-migration equals out-migration, the following equation applies -
Prevalence = Incidence × Duration of disease. Gordis, L. Epidemiology 4th ed. Chapter 3 Saunders Elsevier

questions.question_text:
In a study examining the relationship between domestic abuse and depression, women who do and do not su�er abuse are followed up
over a �ve-year period. It is found that 70 of the 500 individuals who undergo domestic abuse develop depression; 150 of 3000 individuals
who don't get abused develop depression. If the prevalence of domestic abuse in a particular council is 20%, the expected incidence of
depression in this council is
questions.explanation:
It = (Prevalence in the exposed)(Incidence in the exposed) + (1-Prevalence in the exposed)(Incidence in the non-exposed) = (20%)(70/500) +
(1-20%)(150/3000) = 0.068 or 6.8%

questions.question_text:
Cohort studies allow researchers to calculate relative risk and attributable risk. Which of the following statements regarding these measures
is true?

options.text: Attributable risk is a cross product
Attributable risk cannot take negative values
Relative risk cannot take negative values
Attributable risk but not relative risk explains the reason for di�erences between groups

correct_answer.text: Relative risk cannot take negative values

questions.explanation:
Relative risk is a ratio - it can have values less than 1, but not less than 0. Attributable risk is an absolute risk di�erence it can be less than
zero when the risk in exposed is less than the risk in non-exposed. Both attributable risk and relative risk are measures of di�erences
between groups - while the former is an absolute di�erence, the latter is a ratio. The odds ratio is a cross product.

patients were deceased at the time of study. Each patient's social history recorded at the time of admission was scored by two independent

questions.question_text: Which of the following study designs is useful to measure point prevalence of a clinical problem?
questions.explanation:
A cross-section survey assesses the status of an individual with respect to the presence or absence of a disease at a given point in time. It
can be used to assess point prevalence.

questions.question_text: Which of the following study designs is useful to measure the incidence of a clinical problem?
questions.explanation:
Incidence is de�ned by number of new cases. One needs to observe a population long enough to pick all new cases. This is achieved by
cohort studies.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an advantage of case-control design over cohort design?

options.text: Can be used to determine survival rates
Can be used to study prodromal course of a disease
Can explore multiple risk factors for the same disease

correct_answer.text: Can explore multiple risk factors for the same disease

questions.explanation:
Case-control studies are cheaper and faster, compared with other analytic designs. They are useful for studying diseases with long latent
periods. They are useful for studying rare diseases since subjects are selected on the basis of disease status. They allow the investigation of
multiple exposures simultaneously

questions.question_text:
A research team wanted to study the association between an occupational exposure and a relatively rare disease. After much struggle, they
obtain access to the employment records of several major establishments. From these records, the exposures of workers over a period of
10 years are obtained. Using national hospital registry and public health observatory data the researchers determine the cumulative
incidence of disease after exposure in factory workers divided into high, low and no exposure. What type of study is this?
questions.explanation:
As incidence rates are calculated, this study is a cohort study. The subjects are ascertained by exposure status and then the outcome rates
are studied using registries. So this is a retrospective cohort study.
